name: lpddr5
description: LPDDR5 memory controller (JESD209-5) with a UMI front-end and a DFI PHY port; deep per-bank reorder, link SEC-DED ECC, and power management.
authorship: Zero ASIC Corporation; author Andreas Olofsson

human_review.notes: Architecture, feature scope, and per-stage verification directed and reviewed by the author; controller verified stage-by-stage (reorder, ECC, power) and as a full UMI+DFI stack against a JEDEC-checking DFI model.

spec.summary: Synthesizable, technology-agnostic LPDDR5 memory controller. The benchmark top lpddr5_umi wraps the lpddr5 controller with a UMI (SUMI) device endpoint: it unpacks read/write/posted requests into LPDDR5 bursts, tracks per-bank state, schedules a JEDEC-legal command stream honoring the bank-group timing model, and routes read data / write acks back to the requester. The PHY is out of scope and attaches at the DFI boundary. Bank-group mode (NBG groups x NBPG banks); one host request maps to one BL-column burst; all tXXX timings are CK-unit parameters (defaults: a representative LPDDR5-6400 bin).
key_decisions: Build our own pure-RTL controller (not adapt OpenDRAM/UberDDR3/litedram) so it is both ASIC- and FPGA-applicable; the non-portable PHY is excluded and the cut is made at the DFI boundary.

Target a credible JESD209-5 LPDDR5 core: bank-group mode with the full timing set (tRCD/tRP/tRAS/tRC/tRTP/write-recovery/tRRD_S-L/tFAW/tCCD_S-L/tWTR_S-L/tRTW), an all-bank auto-refresh engine (PREA + REFab, tREFI/tRFCab), and an open-page scheduler.

Four production features added: deep per-bank request reorder (per-bank queues, depth QD), link ECC as a (39,32) SEC-DED extended-Hamming lane per 32 data bits, power management (automatic power-down and self-refresh with tXP/tXSR and idle-precharge), and a UMI front-end with per-tag routing context and an output response queue.

Per-bank hardware is modeled with generate (one lpddr5_bank FSM per bank) and saturating down-counters; cross-bank timing lives in the top. No functions in RTL; the ECC column table is a packed constant sliced by genvar (no SV literals).

Verified at the DFI layer with a behavioral LPDDR5 model that both stores/returns ECC-coded data and actively checks the JEDEC timing and power-management protocol, rather than a full PHY + memory-device model.

Read responses are checked order-independently: the bank-group scheduler legitimately reorders reads across banks, so responses are matched back to their request by UMI routing address, not arrival order.

origin.notes: Original implementation written for LogikBench. Follows the JEDEC LPDDR5 command/timing model and the cited DRAM-controller and SEC-DED architectures; not copied from or derived from any specific HDL source.

references: JEDEC JESD209-5, Low Power Double Data Rate 5/5X (LPDDR5/5X) SDRAM Standard.
JEDEC DDR PHY Interface (DFI) Specification, v5.0.
R. W. Hamming, 'Error detecting and error correcting codes,' Bell System Technical Journal, 29(2):147-160, 1950.
B. Jacob, S. W. Ng, D. T. Wang, Memory Systems: Cache, DRAM, Disk, Morgan Kaufmann, 2007.
S. Rixner et al., 'Memory access scheduling,' ISCA, 2000.
